```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(repair)
```

`repair_refit()` rebuilds a MLM, recomputes predictions and their error
covariance, and fits the structural regression again. It first replays the
reference analysis and verifies agreement with the supplied fit. This supports
reproducible sensitivity analyses and provides groundwork for a future person
bootstrap. It currently supports **one MLM**.

## Verify the reference analysis

Keep the original repeated-observation and unit-level data explicitly. The
reference data arguments always describe the original fit, including its
requested scope and structural exclusions.

```{r reference}
data(repair_example)
repeated <- repair_example$repeated
people <- repair_example$people
measurement <- lme4::lmer(
  score ~ day + (day | person), repeated,
  control = lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 100000))
)
fit <- repair(re("day", "growth") ~ practice,
  list(growth = measurement), people, "person", backend = "r")

replay <- repair_refit(
  fit, mlm_data = list(growth = repeated), data = people
)
repair_coefficients(replay)
summary(replay)$refit$checks
```

With no replacement arguments, the returned object is the actual refitted
reference analysis. Identity checks cover effective observations, IDs/grouping,
fixed/random designs, weights and offsets, residual/nuisance and random-effect
covariance, selected predictions, assembled structural inputs, coefficients, and their
covariance. Numerical comparisons use `tolerance = 1e-6`; identity, coding, and
schema checks are exact. A mismatch stops before any replacement fit.

Reference MLM data must retain the fitted observation row names. The
adapter selects the original effective rows by these identities; it does not
re-evaluate old `subset`, `data`, or global-environment expressions. Rows excluded
from the original MLM fit are listed in
`summary(replay)$refit$reference_excluded_rows`. Structural exclusion reasons remain
in `repair_diagnostics(replay, "excluded")`.

## Fit explicitly changed data or a revised scope

Use the separate `new_mlm_data` and `new_data` arguments for replacements.
Omitting either replacement argument retains its reference inputs. For example,
restrict both MLM fitting and structural analysis to 50 people:

```{r replacement}
revised_people <- people[1:50, ]
revised_repeated <- repeated[repeated$person %in% revised_people$person, ]
revised <- repair_refit(
  fit, mlm_data = repeated, data = people,
  new_mlm_data = revised_repeated, new_data = revised_people
)
repair_coefficients(revised)
summary(revised)$refit$checks
```

This estimates the complete procedure on the revised scope. Keeping all original
measurement people while changing only `new_data` defines a different analysis;
choose the intended MLM scope explicitly.

Every supplied replacement measurement row must be used in its original order.
Missing used values, implicit callback subsetting, or omission cause an error.
Replacement structural data use the strict `na_action = "fail"` policy. Prepare a
complete, substantively chosen scope before refitting. The original structural
formula, computation backend, and regularization policy/custom alpha are retained;
sample-dependent moments and weights are recomputed.

Fixed factor coding is frozen from the reference fit. Missing or new levels and
changed coefficient schemas fail explicitly rather than silently changing what a
coefficient means. Newly created fits record structural factor matrices for this
purpose. For older saved fits without that metadata, reference replay must first
establish the original coding from the supplied reference data.

## What the native adapters preserve

| Component | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Measurement backend | Gaussian lmer or supported single-group linear lme |
| Formula and target | Same fixed/random coefficient schema and target grouping; contained lmer nuisance groups remain supported |
| ML/REML | Recorded method retained and checked |
| Weights/offsets | Data-only expressions rebuilt on the supplied rows; global vectors require an explicit recipe |
| Contrasts | Recorded fixed-factor matrices and levels retained; incompatible levels fail |
| lmer optimizer | Recorded optimizer and optimizer controls checked |
| Literal control recipes | Reconstructed with supported constructors; recorded recipes compared |
| nlme covariance | Supported AR(1)/CAR(1), varIdent/varPower, random covariance classes and fixed constraints checked |
| Shared nuisance groups | Rejected by the ordinary structural validator |

Native expressions use explicit columns and a small deterministic grammar.
Ordinary arithmetic, `I`, `offset`, basic log/square-root transforms, and grouping
operators are supported. Sample-dependent `scale`/`poly`, arbitrary functions,
symbolic controls, and other external dependencies require an explicit fitting
function. Precompute transformed columns when possible. Random-only categorical
slopes and transformed factor coding also require an explicit recipe.

The native adapter preserves recorded choices; fitted objects cannot recover
every historical global default or an external control object's earlier value.
The audit's `controls` column distinguishes `recorded_recipe`,
`recorded_optimizer` (lmer's retained optimizer settings), and
`callback_declared` (unrecoverable nlme controls declared by the caller's recipe).
Identity agreement verifies the reference calculation, not unrecorded settings.

## Supply an explicit fitting recipe when needed

`refitter` is a deterministic function accepting **one effective MLM data
frame** and returning its fitted model. It runs for both reference and replacement
inputs and is checked for method, rows, specification, and coefficient identities.
The caller must supply the original fitting choices that the backend did not
retain. In particular, do not use a callback to hide convergence failures.

```{r callback}
recipe <- function(data) {
  lme4::lmer(score ~ day + (day | person), data,
    control = lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 100000)))
}
explicit <- repair_refit(fit, repeated, people, refitter = recipe)
summary(explicit)$refit$checks
```

Measurement failures stop with the reference/replacement stage identified.
A singular random-effect covariance can be retained when convergence, prediction extraction,
and structural estimation remain usable. Warnings and messages are recorded in
`summary(result)$refit$warnings` and `$messages`; informational warnings are not
blanket failures. Available optimizer failure codes and convergence warnings are
fatal. Inspect recorded warnings before interpreting a refitted analysis.

## Replay a deterministic list of whole people

`draw` accepts source IDs with repeats. It makes **no random sample** and does not
produce bootstrap SEs or intervals. This example omits the first source person
and includes the second twice:

```{r draw}
sources <- c(people$person[-1], people$person[2])
copied <- repair_refit(fit, repeated, people, draw = sources)
head(summary(copied)$refit$draw)
summary(copied)$refit$checks
```

Every occurrence gets a new target identity. All of that source person's
effective observations and its structural row are copied together. Character
source IDs such as `"001"` are preserved in a separate mapping rather than parsed
from generated names. `draw` requires identical MLM and structural scopes;
measurement-only people, including those omitted structurally despite having
MLM data, require an explicitly revised reference fit before using this
convenience interface. It cannot be combined
with replacement data.

For nested nuisance effects, `person:day` is recomputed from each fresh person ID,
while standalone nuisance ID columns are also re-keyed. Merely copying records
without new IDs could merge two occurrences into one cluster or introduce shared
nuisance effects. The convenience interface requires a bare target ID column and
nuisance groups expressed as bare ID columns or expressions containing the target.
IDs also used as substantive covariates cannot be re-keyed automatically; supply
explicit replacement data for unsupported mappings.

```{r nested-draw}
reference <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "nested-workflow-reference.rds", package = "repair"))
example <- reference$cases$nested_intercept
model <- lme4::lmer(y ~ x + offset(off) + (x | person) + (1 | person:day),
  example$data, weights = prior, na.action = na.exclude,
  control = lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 100000)))
nested <- repair(
  re("x", "growth", "person") ~ re("(Intercept)", "growth", "person") + practice,
  list(growth = model), example$people, "person"
)
ids <- c(example$people$person[-1], example$people$person[2])
refitted <- repair_refit(nested, example$data, example$people, draw = ids)
repair_coefficients(refitted)
```

## Current boundary and reproducibility

Results are ordinary REPAIR fits: use the existing generics and table extractors.
The original fit remains the reference. Refitted models retain explicit fitting
data in their model/formula environment; the audit records versions, counts,
warnings and any deterministic source-ID mapping. Save analysis code, inputs,
`sessionInfo()`, and result tables along with serialized objects.

Multiple MLMs and supplied cross-model covariance replay remain
outside this increment. Random bootstrap sampling, replicate management,
bootstrap uncertainty, parallel execution, and coverage validation are future
work. A refitted object's standard errors remain the conditional model-based
standard errors of that fit.
